title: Numerical Integration
description: Trapezoidal and Simpson's rule, Newton–Cotes, composite rules, error order, Romberg extrapolation, Gaussian quadrature.
html:
📊 Numerical Integration

1. Quadrature Formulas

$$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx \approx \sum_{i} w_i f(x_i), \qquad \text{degree of exactness } m: \text{ exact for all polynomials up to degree } m$$

Basic formulas on $[a,b]$

Trapezoid $T = \frac{b-a}{2}(f_a + f_b)$ (degree 1), midpoint $M = (b-a)f_m$ (degree 1), Simpson $S = \frac{b-a}{6}(f_a + 4f_m + f_b)$ (degree 3), $S = \frac{2M + T}{3}$.

Example $\int_0^1 e^x\,dx = 1.718282$

$T = 1.859141$, $M = 1.648721$, $S = 1.718861$, 2-point Gauss $= 1.717896$.

2. Composite Rules and Error

$$T(h) = h\bigl(\tfrac12 f_0 + f_1 + \dots + f_{n-1} + \tfrac12 f_n\bigr), \quad S(h) = \tfrac h3\bigl(f_0 + 4f_1 + 2f_2 + \dots + 4f_{n-1} + f_n\bigr)$$

$$E_T = -\frac{b-a}{12}h^2f''(\xi), \qquad E_S = -\frac{b-a}{180}h^4f^{(4)}(\xi)$$

Half step size: trapezoidal error $/4$, Simpson error $/16$. $h = (b-a)/n$; Simpson needs even $n$.

3. Romberg and Gauss

$$R_{k,j+1} = \frac{4^jR_{k,j} - R_{k-1,j}}{4^j - 1}, \qquad \frac{4T(h/2) - T(h)}{3} = S(h)$$

Gauss with $n$ nodes: degree of exactness $2n-1$, weights positive. 2-point on $[-1,1]$: nodes $\pm\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$, weights $1$. Transformation: $x = \frac{b-a}{2}t + \frac{a+b}{2}$.

4. Adaptive and Practical Hints

  • Simpson error estimate: $|I - S_2| \approx |S_2 - S_1|/15$.
  • Remove singularities beforehand by substitution; periodic functions: trapezoidal rule.
  • Avoid high Newton–Cotes orders (negative weights).

5. Typical Mistakes

  • Simpson with an odd number of subintervals.
  • Confusing $h$ with the number of subintervals.
  • Forgetting the end weights $\frac12$ in the composite trapezoidal rule.
